title: Food Safety at Home
hook: Most food poisoning starts in an ordinary kitchen. Four simple habits — clean, separate, cook, chill — prevent the great majority of it.
key_points: Clean: wash hands, utensils, and surfaces often when handling food.
Separate: keep raw meat, poultry, and seafood away from ready-to-eat foods.
Cook: use a food thermometer to reach safe internal temperatures.
Chill: refrigerate perishables promptly, within two hours (one in the heat).
content_html: You don't need a restaurant kitchen to give yourself food poisoning — most cases trace back to the home. The good news is that the official guidance boils down to four words anyone can remember.
extra_html: FoodSafety.gov, run by the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, organizes home food safety around four steps. Clean: wash your hands and sanitize surfaces and utensils frequently, and rinse produce. Separate: keep raw meat, poultry, seafood, and their juices away from foods that won't be cooked, using different cutting boards to avoid cross-contamination. Cook: heat foods to safe internal temperatures, checked with a food thermometer rather than guessed by color. Chill: refrigerate perishables promptly — within two hours, or one hour when it's hotter than 90°F — and thaw frozen food in the fridge, not on the counter. Bacteria multiply fastest in the "danger zone" between about 40°F and 140°F, and these four habits are designed to keep food out of it.

related.title: Handwashing: The Cheapest Medicine
related.hook: It sounds almost too simple, but washing your hands well is one of the most effective things you can do to stop the spread of illness in a household.

related.title: Fifteen Years of Produce Safety Rules, and Outbreaks Keep Coming
related.hook: The FDA wrote real rules for how farms grow your salad. The problem is almost nobody checks whether farms follow them — some have never had a single inspection.

flashcards.prompt: What are the four steps to food safety?
flashcards.back_html: Clean, Separate, Cook, Chill — wash often, keep raw meat apart from ready-to-eat food, cook to safe temperatures, and refrigerate promptly.

flashcards.prompt: How soon should perishable food be refrigerated?

choices.text: Within 2 hours (1 hour if it's hot out)

flashcards.explanation_html: FoodSafety.gov advises refrigerating perishables within 2 hours — or within 1 hour if the temperature is above 90°F (32°C) — to keep bacteria from multiplying.
